assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction broke a limit on electron lenses that had stood since Scherzer's 1936 theorem and brought sub-angstrom imaging of atoms to routine materials physics. It is a true instrument breakthrough with a huge downstream footprint, which is the kind of enabling measurement tool I value.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the optical design, Haider led the hexapole corrector realization, and Urban led the Julich implementation and demonstration. The three-way split is natural and fits the credited names exactly. Other groups (e.g. Krivanek and colleagues with quadrupole-octupole correctors) have claims that the supplied credit omits.
assessment.maturity: About 25 years of use across many independent labs and instrument vendors; the impact is long settled and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Krivanek and the Nion approach are outside the credited names, so the priority question is not fully clean.
Committee may see this as chemistry or materials instrumentation rather than physics; I am relying on general knowledge of the history and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson at the LHC in 2012 completed the Standard Model and was an extraordinary detector, trigger and analysis achievement. Its physics is lasting, and the 2013 prize recognised the theory but not the experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions were made by thousands of people in two collaborations. A fair three-person configuration is hard; the founding spokespersons and project leaders (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) and the 2012 spokesperson Gianotti are the most defensible choices, but any selection leaves out Della Negra or others and is open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: independent confirmation by two experiments, later coupling and spin-parity measurements, and more than a decade of follow-up. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Rules limit the prize to three people, so a collaboration-scale discovery forces a contestable choice among four credited names.
Whether the committee would reward individuals for a collective detector effort is a matter of precedent and judgement, not evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainty around 1e-18 and underpins redefinition of the second, geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. It is a precision-measurement instrument with a clear, lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated it; Ye led the development to the highest accuracy and stability and the broader spectroscopy programme. Both are clearly decisive and the pair is a clean configuration. Ion-clock work (Wineland, Hall-Hansch combs already recognised) is separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent clocks worldwide agree at the 1e-18 level and the redefinition of the second is under discussion; timing is good.
uncertainties: Strontium versus ytterbium versus other species and the relative weight of Sr-clock contributions from other groups (e.g. Lemonde and Ludlow and Oates) are not resolved by the supplied credit.
I have not verified specific accuracy records myself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, plus the TXS 0506+056 association in 2018 and the Galactic-plane result in 2023, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. Building a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice was a remarkable instrumental achievement in my own field.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube project and Karle was a central figure in the detector and its ice calibration. Both fit the credited names, though the project involved a large collaboration and other early pioneers (AMANDA, DUMAND, Baikal) are not credited, so the allocation is not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: the diffuse flux is confirmed by other channels and analyses, but source identification is still thin (one or two sources) and the cosmic-ray origin question is unresolved. Recognition could be argued as slightly early.
uncertainties: Few firmly identified sources; interpretation of the astrophysical flux is still evolving.
KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD have not yet independently confirmed at high significance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision mapping of the CMB anisotropies and the acoustic peak structure fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level. This is among the most important measurements in modern cosmology, although COBE already received the prize in 2006 and the committee will ask what is new.
assessment.attribution: WMAP leadership (Bennett as PI, Page and Spergel in key instrument and analysis roles) is a natural trio. Planck (Puget) and the balloon experiments, and theory by Sunyaev and others, make the credit contestable, and I would worry about leaving out the balloon and ground-based pioneers.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; WMAP and Planck independently agree and the parameters are stable, so recognition is more than timely.
uncertainties: The Planck and balloon-experiment contributions complicate a clean division.
Whether the committee regards the 2006 and 2019 prizes as having already covered this area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2019 M87* and 2022 Sgr A* images gave the first direct, horizon-scale evidence of black-hole shadows. The very-long-baseline interferometry achievement at 1.3 mm, with its calibration and imaging-reconstruction challenges, is impressive observational technology.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea, Doeleman led the EHT collaboration and the technical VLBI development, and Zensus led the European and MPIfR contribution. A large collaboration complicates this and the theory of the shadow has earlier roots.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: two sources imaged and subsequent polarisation and multi-epoch results are consistent, but independent confirmation by a different instrument is still lacking and image-reconstruction systematics remain debated. Slightly early.
uncertainties: Dependence on reconstruction algorithms and priors, and absence of an independent array.
Attribution to three individuals underplays a collaboration of hundreds.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a whole field of topological band physics. I rely on colleagues for condensed-matter judgement, but the originality and breadth look very large.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, and Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. BHZ and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hasan) are not in the credited names, so the allocation is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent materials confirmations over more than 15 years; the 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions, so the field is already partly recognised.
uncertainties: Credit boundaries with BHZ and 3D topological insulators are unresolved.
Outside my expertise; I defer to the condensed-matter members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence in 2023 for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave window and rests on long-term timing precision, an instrument-and-calibration effort I respect.
assessment.attribution: Several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA) found consistent results; credit across the four named people covers some of the founding and leadership contributions but not all, and Manchester's role in Parkes timing could equally be argued.
assessment.maturity: Probably premature: the evidence is around 3-4 sigma for Hellings-Downs correlation, the source (supermassive binaries versus new physics) is unresolved, and the detection is not yet at discovery significance.
uncertainties: Significance and astrophysical origin remain open.
Choosing three of four credited names is arbitrary and the collaboration structure makes credit contentious.
